newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CC-Amatil says drinks deal will boost EPS.
newsitem.headline: CC-Amatil says drinks deal will boost EPS.

text.p: An A$3.4 billion soft drink deal with San Miguel of the Philippines would lead to an increase in Coca-Cola Amatil's earnings per share, C-C Amatil chairman Dean Wills said on Thursday.
Wills told reporters he had stated earlier at the annual general meeting that C-C Amatil would have an enhanced net profit result for 1997.

"If you look at that and then you look at the achievements of CCBPI, and add the two together and divide by the total number of shares, you should come out with a substantial increase in earnings per share," he said.
C-C Amatil earlier announced it would issue 293 million shares to acquire San Miguel soft drink subsidiary Coca Cola Bottler Philippines Inc (CCBPI).
CCBPI earned a net profit of A$144 million in 1996, struck on sales of A$1.2 billion. This compared with C-C Amatil's net profit of A$142 million, on sales on of A$3.7 billion.
CCBPI is 70 percent owned by San Miguel and 30 percent owned by The Coca Cola Company.
Wills also told a briefing the deal would strengthen C-C Amatil's balance sheet.
The company's debt to equity ratio, at 54.6 percent in 1996, would be about halved on 1996 figures, said executive director corporate development John Priest.
CCBPI had very little debt, enabling CC-Amatil to considerable strengthen its balance sheet and improve its borrowing capacity, Priest said.
Wills said the agreement was subject to shareholder approval and should be considered at a shareholder meeting in June.
